conclusion: Use bounded correlated steering for one swarm entity, not independent random direction every frame or full flocking/pathfinding for every fly.
godot_answer: Godot supplies collision movement, navigation paths, avoidance and random navigable-point queries; game code still selects wander goals/steering and moves the actor. NavigationAgent2D is not a finished wandering AI.

sources.title: Craig Reynolds: Wander steering behavior
sources.finding: Retaining and perturbing a wander direction creates coherent random motion. Unrelated random headings each frame lack that continuity.

sources.title: GameMaker: New Enemy in Windy Woods (2D platformer)
sources.finding: Tutorial demonstrates timed random jump direction then replaces it with targeted motion for predictability. Transfer the lesson about legible timing, not its player pursuit, which conflicts with our approved flies.

sources.title: GameMaker: Hero’s Trail overview (2D action-adventure, not a platformer)
sources.finding: Authored paths constrain enemies and animation uses actual movement direction. Supports deliberate encounter space and velocity-driven animation; not evidence that random wandering is mandatory.

sources.title: Godot: Using NavigationAgents
sources.finding: Agents provide path-following data but user code moves actors. Avoidance has no knowledge of physics collision; it cannot replace collision checks.

sources.title: Godot: NavigationServer2D
sources.finding: Random points can be sampled from navigation polygons. Useful for maze-like routing, unnecessary for a few swarms in simple authored flight regions.

sources.title: Godot: Using CharacterBody2D/3D
sources.finding: Movement/collision APIs support custom behavior. Reuse the project collision architecture rather than impose a scene-tree conversion for this feature.

decision: Keep existing project toolchain. Implement a small stateful steering routine, explicit collision, authored flight bounds, and one collision entity per swarm. Consider navigation only if later level geometry needs routing.
confidence: Principles are supported by sources; tuning numbers and placement choices are our first-pass design, not source-prescribed or playtested guarantees.
validation: Physics-tick seeded tests independent of render FPS, many seeds in corners and near doors; visual evaluation still required.
